title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 216: Bioprospecting in the Cryosphere
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 216 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Bioprospecting in the Cryosphere: The Cold Search for Novel Antibiotics

Paragraph 1. Hospitals around the world face a big health problem today. For many years, doctors and farmers used too many antibiotics. Because of this overuse, dangerous bacteria changed and stopped dying from old medicines. The World Health Organization warns that drug-resistant germs could cause ten million deaths a year by 2050. For seventy years, scientists found most antibiotics in farm soil, but now that soil holds almost nothing new.

Paragraph 2. To find fresh medicines, researchers are now searching freezing parts of the planet, like glaciers and Antarctic ice. This frozen world is full of tiny cold-loving bacteria called psychrophiles. Biologist Dr. Rebecca Frost explains that these germs make special flexible chemicals to stay alive in extreme cold. Because these chemicals attack rival germs in ice pockets, they could become powerful new antibiotics for humans.

Paragraph 3. Scientist Dr. Liam Chen led a trip to Greenland and drilled four hundred metres deep into ancient ice. His team found over two hundred kinds of cold bacteria. In lab tests, chemicals from one new bacterium broke through the protective wall around a dangerous hospital germ called MRSA, killing it completely.

Paragraph 4. Still, turning ice bacteria into factory medicine is difficult. These cold germs die quickly if factory tanks become warmer than ten degrees Celsius, so cooling giant tanks costs huge amounts of money. Also, as Earth gets warmer and glaciers melt away, many useful ice germs may disappear forever before scientists can save them.

groups.title: Questions 1–4
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: Why did old antibiotic medicines stop working well against some bacteria?
options: A. Factories stopped making medicine for farms.
B. Cold weather froze most hospital antibiotics.
C. Doctors and farmers used antibiotics too much.

steps: Đoạn 1: Do bác sĩ và nông dân lạm dụng thuốc kháng sinh quá nhiều.

options: A. Tiny bacteria that live happily in freezing places
B. Special tools used to drill deep ice holes
C. Dangerous viruses found in warm farm soil

steps: Đoạn 2: Vi khuẩn nhỏ bé ưa lạnh sống ở vùng băng giá.

q3.text: Where did Dr. Liam Chen drill 400 metres deep to find ancient bacteria?

steps: Đoạn 3: "...led a trip to Greenland and drilled four hundred metres deep into ancient ice."

q4.text: Why is it expensive to grow cold bacteria inside medicine factories?
options: A. They need expensive farm soil to survive.
B. They break glass tanks with sharp ice.
C. Giant tanks must stay colder than ten degrees Celsius.

steps: Đoạn 4: Vi khuẩn chết nếu ấm hơn 10 độ C, làm lạnh bồn lớn rất tốn tiền.

q5.text: Dr. Rebecca Frost spent ten winters living inside an Antarctic research camp.

steps: Đoạn 2: Chỉ nêu giải thích của Dr. Frost, không nhắc bà sống ở Nam Cực 10 mùa đông.

q6.text: Farm soil still provides plenty of brand-new antibiotics every year.

steps: Đoạn 1: Đất nông nghiệp hiện hầu như không còn gì mới (holds almost nothing new).

q7.text: A germ found in Greenland ice broke through the protective shield of MRSA.

steps: Đoạn 3: Hóa chất từ vi khuẩn mới phá vỡ lớp vỏ bảo vệ của MRSA.

q8.text: Cold bacteria grow fastest when factory tanks are heated to warm temperatures.

steps: Đoạn 4: Chúng chết nhanh nếu bồn ấm hơn 10 độ C (die quickly if factory tanks become warmer).
